title: Free Kart game for kids
author: Zeromizer22
selftext:
This is made for me and my partner's kid to play. He loves pokemon, minecraft and Lego and thought we could have some fun together. Its not for commercial, so just sharing if others are interested to play with their kids.

[https://pokemon-star-kart.vercel.app/](https://pokemon-star-kart.vercel.app/)

comments.author: ArialBear
comments.body:
Why call down the wrath of nintendo? Lol. Looks fun either way

Edit: after playing it was really fun. Love the weapon set up and the pokemon obstacles

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body:
Pokemon Batman LEGO Minecraft... yeah, that's more than just Nintendo.

I'm missing some Mickey GTA Sims Roblox, though.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Wow, I’m jealous that you made a Pokemon game that is way better that what I’m currently making…

comments.author: Ukawok92
comments.body: why make it pokemon themed? if nintendo finds out they will shut you down.

replies.author: PositiveScarcity8909
replies.body:
Shut down what? The files in his computer?

He is not selling anything.

replies.author: Ukawok92
replies.body:
Don't think Nintendo cares about that. He's using their IP in a way they don't want.

It a small game so they are probably fine, but this something I wouldn't risk.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Once the files are on the internet and free, there’s not much they can do. They can take down all copies of it and as long as someone downloaded them, the minute they take their eyes off this game it goes straight back up. Or it’s just hidden deeper than a google search.

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body: Feel free to test that theory, it's a teachable opportunity about how lawsuits work.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body:
Please teach me now I’m curious. Let’s say the files ended up in the hands of someone in Congo for example. They upload them using a VPN set to the Philippines to a website that isn’t in Googles database and post the link in a discord you have to get approved to join.

How do they realistically prevent a free game getting shared in this way? Do they even care enough for that? How are they finding the person who shared the files and can they even sue that person in that country?

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body:
They prevent it the same way that capital punishment prevents society from commiting crimes: they sue you into the ground as a cautionary tale.

Nobody cares what someone in their own backyard in Congo does with whatever files, what they care about is keeping a distinctive trademark, which *requires* them to sue anyone who might dilute them, and sending a message to anyone who even thinks about skirting the law... plus, theor law firm cares about provinh how active they are, so they'll sue anyone, even a homeless bankrupt, just to rack up billable hours.

You want to go live in Congo? Cool. There's also plenty of FTP servers in Iran with all kinds of pirated software, maybe you'd rather live there? You think you can hide behind VPNs and Discord (a US company that has to hand out data when requested)? Sure, you can test that theory too, let's see how long you can truly hide.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body:
Are you confusing me with OP? You keep saying things like see how I get on with it and stuff. I don’t have these files and I’m never going to distribute them.

And you’re missing the point. I don’t have to go live in Congo to do all that. There’s already millions of people there. As soon as the files go onto the internet once, anyone can download them. By the time the first lawsuit starts those files could be in the hands of hundreds of thousands of people all across the world in places Nintendo can’t reach. You are significantly overestimating the power of one companies ability to sue.

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body:
I'm not overestimating anything: better avoid any country that's a signatory of the Berne Convention, particularly those where Nintendo has offices, if you don't want to meet their lawyers. Yes, that leaves you with some safe heavens, pick one.

Oh, right, you don't have the files... you want *someone else* to make and upload them so you can have them? Are they cool with that?... and you still want to end up with the files, so yeah, strengthen up that opsec.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body:
Mate you’re thinking about this too deeply and involving me too much. This is a hypothetical.

Case in point to prove it once and for all: every single Nintendo game is online for free and can be pirated. You think these super lawyers can stop this free game if they can’t even stop their own paid games being online? Come on bro.

replies.author: EmergencyArm4610
replies.body: Why try to enforce nintendo copyright? I dont get these comments.

replies.author: EasyTarget973
replies.body: no kidding

replies.author: Ukawok92
replies.body: Who's trying? Just seems silly to use Nintendo IP to me.

replies.author: Iggyhopper
replies.body: If anything becomes popular enough, free or not, Nintendo is *definitely* knocking.

replies.author: Ukawok92
replies.body: Yeah that's what I'm saying, exactly!

replies.author: EmergencyArm4610
replies.body: Let Nintendo spend money on that. Discouraging people from creating non revenue generating content just makes it easier for nintendo. Its questionable that companys should be able to take down stuff that isnt making money and its not illegal to make stuff like OP but yes it could be a target for companies that have the resources to go after them.

replies.author: MilaKunisWatermelon
replies.body:
Because IP infringement cuts both ways. Without these laws, indie devs stand no chance against large corporations. 

Nintendo would have just stolen the name “Stardew Valley” and slapped it on Story of Seasons the moment it gained traction. Xbox would have just stolen Minecraft instead of paying $2.5 billion for it.

replies.author: EmergencyArm4610
replies.body: OP isnt charging anything. This is fair use.

replies.author: MilaKunisWatermelon
replies.body: lol you don’t know what fair use is. Using someone else’s IP is not fair use, even if you don’t charge anything.

replies.author: Ukawok92
replies.body: That is not how fair use works lol

comments.author: pirondi
comments.body: Wow where do i sign to play this and get sued together? haha

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body: You won't get sued for just playing it. Releasing it... that's a different matter.

comments.author: readytojumpstart
comments.body:
Everyone in this thread thinks nintendo owns pokemon.  

You shouldnt be developing games if you think this

replies.author: Quirky-Split7157
replies.body: Nintendo is the publisher of the games, own approx 1/3 of the pokemon company and also holds key trademark patents as well as software patents. Get off your high horse.

replies.author: MilaKunisWatermelon
replies.body:
Nintendo had Pokémon Uranium shut down, if this gets any sort of popularity at all they will have this shut down too.

And yes, Nintendo has a stake in Pokemon. They don’t own it outright, but they do get involved in taking down things that use the IP.

You shouldn’t be speaking about IP infringement or game development at all because you have no clue about anything on the subject.

replies.body:
